review_evidence: src/FOLP/IFOLP.thy: typedecls p/o, consts for connectives and proof-term formers, axiomatizations (ieqI, conjI, disjE, impI, allI, exI, proof-equality rules), definitions Not/iff/Ex1, and about 60 schematic_goal derivations (conjE, iffI, subst, sym, conj_cong, rewrite-rule sets).
src/FOLP/FOLP.thy: axiomatization of cla/classical plus schematic_goal proofs disjCI, ex_classical, exCI, excluded_middle, impCE, notnotD, iffCE, swap, cla_rews.
src/FOLP/ex/Classical.thy: about 60 proved schematic goals, including Pelletier problems 1-60 in classical FOL with proof terms.
src/FOLP/ex/Intuitionistic.thy: intuitionistic double-negation lemmas and Pelletier problems, proved with IntPr.fast_tac/best_tac, and oops'd non-constructive goals.
src/FOLP/ex/Foundation.thy, Intro.thy, If.thy: step-by-step natural-deduction proofs; If.thy defines if(P,Q,R) and proves ifI, ifE, if_commute, nested_ifs.
src/FOLP/ex/Nat.thy: Peano axiomatization (induct, Suc_inject, rec_0, rec_Suc), definition add, proofs Suc_n_not_n, add_0, add_Suc, add_assoc, add_0_right, add_Suc_right.

src/FOLP/ex/Propositional_Cla.thy, Propositional_Int.thy, Quantifiers_Cla.thy, Quantifiers_Int.thy: 20 to 30 named or anonymous schematic goals each (stab_imp, peirce_imp1, mints, tatsuta; quantifier laws from Principia Mathematica *11.53, *11.55, *11.61).

src/LCF/LCF.thy: class cpo, typedecls tr/void/prod/sum, domain-theory axiomatizations (less_trans, FIX_eq, induct, adm_* rules), and about 50 lemmas (less_anti_sym, ext, COND_cases, PROD_less, least_FIX, lfp_is_FIX, FIX_pair, induct2).

src/LCF/ex/Ex1.thy to Ex4.thy: fixpoint-induction examples; each file has axiomatizations or a lemma: H_idemp (Ex1), example on F and H (Ex2), p(FIX(s),y)=FIX(s) (Ex3), FIX(f)=p for a least prefixpoint (Ex4).
summary: Read all 17 .thy files in full (FOLP core, 10 FOLP examples, LCF core, 4 LCF examples). Every file declares a theory and holds formal statements with proofs, axiomatizations, or definitions of logic with proof terms (FOLP) or domain theory (LCF). No file is import-only or free of formal content, so all 17 stay searchable; no exclusions.
